label: Game B
nuance_found: Timing the lance: hold Couch too early and you lose footing, too late and you eat the hit, in the gold band you strike clean. Layered on that: charge your lance under a storm cell (lance up), hit from high ground or off a crest for more damage, and each rival has a different habit (rammer, long lance, line-switchers, lightning caller) so I had to change how I approached each one.
audio: Bright regatta music loop, plus thunder, lance cracks, body thuds, horn and jump sounds on every action; rival taunts in speech bubbles. Always something to hear.
furthest_progress: Beat all 8 rivals in the Squall Cup (Pip, Barnacle, Doc Volta, Contessa Brisa, Kite, Gilly Twins, Lady Marrow, Admiral Nimbus) and got SQUALL CUP CHAMPION at 2,500 points around 508 s, then started a rematch.
control_trouble: Steering with my thumb in 0.5 s snapshots made the early jousts hit-and-miss, and I mistimed the first two couches. Mostly my clumsy timing, not the game, since the gold-band bar and the orange ring tell you exactly when to press.
best_moment: Landing a charged lance on the Admiral for the Squall Cup win, with BOTH HIT sparks flying and the music kicking.
worst_moment: Dying to Brisa and the Admiral on a rematch with no obvious way to know why, and the camera swooping inside masts so I could not see the target for a second.
verdict: Right, this is a game. Within 25 seconds I knew what to do: sail at the other boat, hold the red button at the right moment. Every hit has a big BOTH HIT or LATE COUCH pop, the boats are gorgeous, the music is jolly and each opponent talks back. A match is 30 to 60 seconds, which is exactly a bus gap, and winning gives me a new boat or lance to equip, so I wanted the next rival. The camera sometimes flies inside a mast and the first match explains little, but I would play this again this week and probably tell someone about it.
